findings.title: Regression: Symlink Protections Reverted in SGX SDK/DCAP Enables Arbitrary File Read/Write and Library Injection

affected_components.issue: dlopen(qpl_path) - arbitrary library load via public API sgx_ql_set_path
open(filename, O_CREAT|O_RDWR, 0666) - bypasses protected FS isolation
fopen(full_path, wb/rb) - AESM persistent storage symlink follow

findings.mitigation_check: ZERO mitigations (O_NOFOLLOW, openat2, RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, safe_open) found in HEAD or any branch post-revert
findings.scope_verification: IN SCOPE - Software (Tier 3) / Firmware (Tier 2). IT Infrastructure explicitly excluded.
findings.poc_concept: Non-destructive: Place symlink in user-writable QCNL cache dir (~/.dcap-qcnl/) pointing to sensitive file → next cache operation reads/writes target. For QPL: call sgx_ql_set_path() with attacker-controlled path → dlopen loads arbitrary .so at quote generation time.
aggravating_factors: World-writable cache dir (0777) lowers multi-user exploitation barrier
QPL path settable via public exported API from untrusted app context
Protected FS mode 0666 combined with symlink follow defeats isolation guarantee

notes: Pivoted from NVIDIA. Intel program uses UUID-based API. Tier 1 is Hardware only. Max bounty 100k USD. Requires physical/emulated testbed for SGX/TDX/ME research.

testing_constraints.notes: Tier 1 Hardware requires physical board or emulated platform. No web endpoints in scope except documentation.

human_gate_summary.evidence_sufficiency: Complete - commit hashes, file:line references, absence of mitigations verified across all branches
